“Local deployment of models offers a way to mitigate some privacy risks while still maintaining essential data protection responsibilities.  Instead of sending data to a central server, you can run the model directly on your own infrastructure. This reduces the risk of exposure because the data never leaves your environment. However, it’s crucial to remember that this approach doesn’t eliminate all data protection obligations.  You still need to carefully consider the specific deployment contexts and potential threats.

To achieve this, other privacy-enhancing techniques exist. These methods allow you to retrieve predictions or classifications without revealing *all* the underlying data.  Essentially, they provide a way to get an answer without fully exposing the question itself.  This is particularly important when deploying models in situations where full disclosure would be problematic.
